subject: pe
topicName: Engagement Patterns in Physical Activity and Sport

steps.title: Engagement patterns
steps.body: The ways in which different groups of people participate (or don't participate) in physical activity and sport. These patterns vary significantly based on personal, social and cultural factors.

steps.title: Key Point
steps.body: The process of socialisation means that children learn attitudes and behaviours from their family. A child raised in a sporty family is far more likely to participate in sport than one whose family has no interest in physical activity. This influence is especially strong in early childhood.

steps.title: PE Exam Tips — Engagement Patterns in Physical Activity and Sport
steps.body: 1. For Engagement Patterns in Physical Activity and Sport questions, use subject-specific terminology precisely 2. Support every point with specific evidence or examples 3. Show balanced analysis — consider different perspectives before reaching a conclusion 4. Link your understanding of Engagement Patterns in Physical Activity and Sport to real-world contexts where possible 5. For longer answers, plan your response to address all parts of the question

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always explain both the barrier AND a strategy to overcome it - examiners want both Use specific examples for each factor (e.g. Ramadan for religion, not just "religious reasons") Remember that barriers can be practical (cost, transport) or psychological (stereotyping, self-consciousness) When discussing age, address both young people AND older adults Classification in disability sport = fair competition by grouping similar impairments Link socialisation to family influence - this is a key connection examiners look for
